items.description: Permanent fix, as one action: a Jenkins pipeline that takes a deploy repo. One `IaC/Destroy Stage` build, given a deploy repo and a stage, permanently deletes what that retired stage left: its Terraform resources, its state in TerraformState and its `config/<stage>/`. No other step is needed. That holds whatever the stage's state holds: the namespaced Kubernetes objects in it, already gone with the pruned namespace, are dropped from state rather than deleted (Ruling review r1 F1, V20).

The guard fails the build before any Job starts if ArgoCDDeploy's registry on `main` (`releases/values.yaml`; e.g. `fieldnotes` → `https://github.com/pvginkel/FieldnotesDeploy.git` with stage `prd`, `releases/values.yaml:99-102`) has an entry deploying REPO's STAGE, or if a live Application in `argocd-prd` sources REPO with Helm parameter `hook.stage` = STAGE. Single-source and multi-source (`spec.sources[]`) Applications both count. The failure names what still deploys the stage. There is no namespace check.

items.area: R2.2 the Job and the empty configuration
items.description: The pipeline runs the argocd-hook image as a one-off Job in `argocd-hooks`, with the `tf-presync` ServiceAccount and the `argocd-hook-credentials` Secret, under a name no `tf-presync-<namespace>` sync Job can take (`/work/Charts/charts/homelab-shared/templates/_tf-presync-hook.tpl:38`). Its destroy mode clones the deploy repo at a SHA, starts the state backend and inits against `argocd/<repo>/<stage>/terraform.tfstate` (`argocd-hook/presync/backend.py:52-54`). It sets the stage's namespaced Kubernetes objects aside (V20) and plans against a configuration that holds only the root's provider, backend and variable declarations. It passes the stage's tfvars when `config/<stage>/` exists (Ruling review r1 A2). So every other resource in state is an orphan planned for deletion, and `prevent_destroy` no longer binds. A repo whose declarations do not init or plan this way fails the build loudly.

With `APPLY=true` the Job destroys from the plan it saved, checks that the state lists no resources, and then `git rm`s `argocd/<repo>/<stage>/` from TerraformState, using the hook's own `GITHUB_TOKEN`.

With `APPLY=true`, once the Job has succeeded, Jenkins commits `git rm -r config/<stage>` to the deploy repo's `main` with the GitHub credential it uses for version pins (JenkinsPipelineUtils `vars/cicd.groovy:66`).

Each part lands where R2 and Ruling D1 put it: the destroy mode and `Jenkinsfile.destroy-stage` in ArgoCDTools, the grants in ArgoCDDeploy, the dedicated ServiceAccount in JenkinsDeploy, the design as an argo-cd decision in AnsibleSpecs, and a section on the pipeline in this repo's argocd runbook.

items.area: R3 APPLY and the dry run
items.description: An `APPLY` parameter; `APPLY=false` is a dry run. `APPLY` defaults to false. A dry run plans and stops: it shows the destroy plan, lists separately the namespaced Kubernetes objects an apply would forget (Ruling review r1 F1), and names the state file and `config/<stage>/` it would delete. It changes nothing: no resource, no state write, no TerraformState commit, no deploy-repo commit. `APPLY=true` plans and destroys inside the same Job, from the saved plan, with no `input` step.

items.area: R4 / Ruling D3 dev dry run
items.description: FieldnotesDeploy `dev` is the first stage it destroys. The test phase starts `IaC/Destroy Stage` with `APPLY=false` against FieldnotesDeploy `dev`. The plan shows exactly the RBD image `fieldnotes-dev-data` and the PV `fieldnotes-dev-data-pv` for deletion, and the build lists nothing as forgotten. The build names `argocd/FieldnotesDeploy/dev/` (TerraformState holds `argocd/FieldnotesDeploy/dev/terraform.tfstate`, 8120 bytes, at `1b32f10`) and `config/dev/` as what an apply would delete. Afterwards, both are still present.

The test phase starts `IaC/Destroy Stage` once with `APPLY=false` against FieldnotesDeploy `prd`, and the guard fails the build. The registry entry `fieldnotes`/`prd` and the live `fieldnotes-prd` Application, whose `hook.stage` is `prd`, both still deploy that stage.

The operator's `APPLY=true` build against FieldnotesDeploy `dev` leaves the RBD image `fieldnotes-dev-data`, the PV `fieldnotes-dev-data-pv` and `argocd/FieldnotesDeploy/dev/` in TerraformState gone, and `config/dev/` deleted from FieldnotesDeploy (ANS-147's done-when).
items.owed_after: the operator's APPLY=true build of IaC/Destroy Stage against FieldnotesDeploy dev (Ruling D3)

items.description: A new argo-cd decision records the Destroy Stage design and supersedes D28 (`argo-cd/decisions.md:382`), which carries the supersession marker. It carries the narrow overrule of D1 and D33/D41 for this operator-started pipeline only. No existing entry (D1, D27 as amended, D31, D33, D39, D41) is left contradicting it.

The pipeline's cluster work runs as a dedicated ServiceAccount in `jenkins-prd`. It is defined in JenkinsDeploy and named by `Jenkinsfile.destroy-stage`'s pod spec. It is bound to a Role in `argocd-hooks` that holds only what the pipeline's Job lifecycle uses, and to a read-only Role on `argoproj.io` Applications in `argocd-prd`. The shared agent ServiceAccount `jenkins-prd/default` (JenkinsDeploy `chart/templates/jenkins-agent-jobs-rolebinding.yaml:9`) gains nothing. ArgoCDDeploy's render gate pins both grants.

The dedicated ServiceAccount and both of its grants are live on prd before the test phase's dry runs. JenkinsDeploy's `jenkins-prd` Application auto-syncs (live `syncPolicy.automated`). ArgoCDDeploy's chart reaches prd only through a sync of `argocd-prd`, which is not auto-synced (`releases/values.yaml:30`, `autoSync: false`). The test phase syncs `argocd-prd` itself, once, through the elevated `~/.kube/config-prd-write`, and only after a diff of `argocd-prd`'s live state against the pushed ArgoCDDeploy revision shows nothing but this slice's Roles and RoleBindings (on 2026-10-02 `argocd-prd` was `Synced` at `9334541`, ArgoCDDeploy's `origin/main`). If anything else differs it does not sync, and this criterion, V08 and V09 are left owed to the operator.

The destroy mode is a separate entry point of the hook image. The sync hook's four-positional contract (`argocd-hook/presync/cli.py:16-26`), `tests/test_cli.py`'s `ArgumentContractTests`, the Charts render gate and the Charts `hook.imageTag` pin (`"10"`, `charts/homelab-shared/values.yaml:7`) are all unchanged. The pipeline runs `registry:5000/argocd-hook:latest`.

Re-runs are idempotent. An already-empty state skips the destroy, and a state file or `config/<stage>/` folder that is already gone is skipped. Without `config/<stage>/` the Job still reaches its state checks (Ruling review r1 A2), although the sync's own helper refuses such a clone (`argocd-hook/presync/terraform.py:35-37`). A run against a stage with no state file creates none, and a build that stopped halfway is finished by running it again. The hook's unittest suite covers the dry run, the apply, the re-runs, a clone without `config/<stage>/` and an empty configuration that does not plan.

The repository webhook goes with the stage whose state manages it (`manage_webhook`, argo-cd D39). FieldnotesDeploy `dev` does not manage it (`config/dev/terraform.tfvars:4`, `manage_webhook = false`), so its plan shows no webhook.

The job `IaC/Destroy Stage` exists in the `IaC/` folder, created through the Jenkins API to the style guide (Ruling review r1 A1). Its configuration holds only the job, its SCM and its Script Path (JenkinsPipelineUtils `docs/pages/guide/job-properties.md:3-5`). Its parameters come from `Jenkinsfile.destroy-stage` through one parameter-less registration build, and so do its lack of triggers and its refusal of concurrent builds. That build fails on the empty `REPO` before any cluster call and changes nothing. Once registered, the job has no triggers, allows no concurrent builds, and defaults `APPLY` to false. The run starts no build of it except that registration build and Ruling D3's two dry runs.
`Jenkinsfile.destroy-stage` follows the estate's Jenkins pipeline style guide (https://pipelines.home/docs/).

This repo's argocd runbook has a section on destroying a retired stage with the pipeline: when it applies (after undeploy), the dry run first, then the apply, what the guard refuses, and re-running. The undeploy paragraph no longer says that nothing prunes the state (`docs/runbooks/argocd.md:387`).

items.area: Ruling review r1 F1 namespaced objects
items.description: Before planning, the destroy mode drops every Kubernetes object in the stage's state that lives in a namespace from state, without deleting it. Such an object went with the namespace when the Application was pruned, and the Job's identity has no grant left on it. Its only namespaced grant, `tf-presync-app` on Secrets, is bound in the app's own namespace alone (ArgoCDDeploy `chart/templates/hook-namespace.yaml:106-125`, Charts `charts/homelab-shared/templates/_tf-presync-hook.tpl:42-59`). Cluster-scoped objects such as PVs stay in the plan and are destroyed for real, and so is everything outside Kubernetes: databases, buckets, RBD images. A dry run lists the forgotten objects separately, as already gone with the namespace, and still writes nothing. An apply forgets them and destroys the rest. `tf-presync` gains no grant. The hook's unittest suite covers a state that holds a namespaced Secret beside a PV and a resource outside Kubernetes.
